text.tspan: Everyday English - C1 - 2026/10/31 - Phrasal verb -01

svg.title: A route takes time; a departure plan must allow for the journey.

text.tspan: A route takes time; a departure plan must allow for the journey.
factor something in
factor in something
Include a relevant cost, condition or amount of time in a
calculation or decision.
allow for; take into account
When choosing our departure time, we factored in the walk to
the venue and the queue at the entrance.
Separable: factor the delay in / factor in the delay. Put a
pronoun in the middle: factor it in. Often used when planning or
estimating.
A: The lantern walk starts at seven thirty. Leaving at seven
twenty should be fine.
B: Have you factored in the fifteen-minute walk?
A: I hadn’t—and the organizers expect a ten-minute queue.
B: Then let’s work backward from the start time.
The walk starts at 7:30. Getting there takes 15 minutes and
entry takes another 10. What is the latest departure time?
Explain your calculation in one sentence using factor in.
(Model: We should leave by 7:05 because we need to factor in
both the fifteen-minute walk and the ten-minute queue.)
